rows.definition: cmdLoopScore is the cmd/fak entry-point function that parses `fak loop-score` flags (--workspace, --ledger, --registry, --json, --markdown, --compare) and calls internal/loopscore to build/render/compare the loop-durability scorecard payload.
rows.distinction: Not the scorecard's own build/score/render logic (that lives in the internal/loopscore package, the existing loopscore concept) - cmdLoopScore is only the flag-parsing and dispatch shell around it.

rows.definition: codexLoopFailOnExitCode maps a codex-loop diagnosis verdict plus the --fail-on threshold string to the process exit code (0 or 1) that `fak sessions codex-loop` and the dispatch-tick codex gate return, plus whether the threshold parsed.
rows.distinction: Not codexLoopFailOnRank, which only turns the --fail-on threshold NAME into its numeric severity rank with no verdict input, and not codexLoopFailOnName, which only canonicalizes the threshold string for a display message.

rows.definition: codexLoopFailOnName normalizes a --fail-on threshold value to its canonical display name (none|loop|action|unguarded) for the gate-refusal message `fak sessions codex-loop` and the dispatch-tick codex gate print.
rows.distinction: Not codexLoopFailOnRank (which produces the numeric rank used to compare verdicts, not a display string) and not codexLoopFailOnExitCode (which produces a process exit code, not a name).

rows.definition: codexLoopFailOnRank parses a --fail-on threshold string into its ordinal severity rank (or reports it invalid) - the ordering codexLoopFailOnExitCode compares a diagnosis verdict's rank against to decide the gate outcome.
rows.distinction: Not codexLoopFailOnExitCode (which consumes the rank to decide a process exit code) and not codexLoopFailOnName (which renders a display string, not a rank).

rows.definition: The crashloop fence is loopmgr.RestartPolicy: a pure decision core that caps consecutive restart attempts for a supervised loop process, computes a doubling backoff delay with deterministic jitter, and gives up with a typed reason (WATCHDOG_RESTART_EXHAUSTED) instead of letting a failing process restart forever.
rows.distinction: Not doomloop (internal/doomloop), which classifies a WORKER's effort-vs-verified-progress ratio across sample windows; RestartPolicy instead fences how many times a supervised PROCESS may be restarted after it exits, with no notion of progress or effort.

rows.definition: diagnoseCurrentCodexLoop resolves and diagnoses ONE current/most-recent Codex session under a given codex-home directory, returning a codexLoopDiagnosis verdict for the codex_launcher and dispatch-tick codex gate to act on.
rows.distinction: Not diagnoseRecentCodexLoops, which scans and folds MANY recent session files into one aggregate report; this function reads exactly one live session.

rows.definition: diagnoseRecentCodexLoops scans recent Codex session JSONL files under a codex-home directory, bounded by --since-hours/--limit, and folds each into a codexLoopRecentReport carrying per-session diagnoses plus aggregate counts (loop/action/unguarded).
rows.distinction: Not diagnoseCurrentCodexLoop, which diagnoses a single current session; this function is the --recent multi-session batch path used by `fak sessions codex-loop --recent` and the codex gate.

rows.definition: A doom loop is the internal/doomloop VerdictDoomLoop classification: a worker burning effort (transcript lines/turns/tokens) with flat VERIFIED progress (commits/ledger steps) for at least TripWindows consecutive sample windows, correctable by a graduated OBSERVE/NUDGE/ESCALATE ladder that stops below any destructive rung.
rows.distinction: Not the crashloop fence (loopmgr.RestartPolicy), which caps process restart attempts after a crash and has no effort/progress sampling; a doom loop can occur in a process that never crashes at all - it burns effort while staying alive.

rows.definition: KindLoop is the superloop.MemberKind constant tagging a super-loop Member as a ledgered loop id, whose status Walk/Drive reads from the cross-ledger loop-health fold.
rows.distinction: Not KindSuperloop, the sibling MemberKind tagging a member as another super loop - a recursive descend edge in the composition graph, not a leaf loop id.

rows.definition: KindSuperloop is the superloop.MemberKind constant tagging a Member as ANOTHER super loop - the recursion case the composition graph (internal/superloop/graph.go) walks as a descend (out-)edge between intents, feeding the resolves/acyclic/root-rooted/once-only invariants.
rows.distinction: Not KindLoop, which tags a member as a leaf ledgered loop id rather than a nested super loop.

rows.definition: loopDriveOptions is the cmd/fak struct bundling every `fak loop drive` run parameter - goal/ledger/policy paths, loop id, source, principal, iteration/token/deadline caps, the wrapped command, and the optional Lane/Region admission spec consumed by newLoopDriveRegionHold.
rows.distinction: Not the loopdrive package/subsystem itself (the Ralph loop driver that consumes this struct) - loopDriveOptions is only the parameter bag threaded into it, not the drive loop's control flow.

rows.definition: internal/loopunblock is a generic decision core that, given a worst-first worklist head a loop already selected plus its admission status, returns one closed Action (Enter/ClearThenEnter/Bypass/Wait/Escalate/StandDown) so a loop that selected a move it cannot make does not stall the whole queue behind it.
rows.distinction: Not superloop's Walk/Drive, which SELECTS the worst-first head in the first place; loopunblock never selects a candidate, it only decides what to do when the already-selected head is blocked at admission.

rows.definition: MartinLoop (github.com/Keesan12/martin-loop, Apache-2.0) is a third-party governed-agent-run project fak studied via /study-repo + /field-borrow on 2026-07-08, documented in docs/notes/CONCEPT-STUDY-MARTINLOOP-2026-07-08.md, comparing its trust-core modules (leash, test-integrity, grounding, red-blue probes, hash-chained receipts) against fak/DOS and filing 3 genuine gaps as issues #3362-#3364 under epic #2871.
rows.distinction: Not one of fak's own loop subsystems (loop/superloop/loopmgr/etc.) - MartinLoop is an external sibling project fak read for field-borrow candidates; none were vendored, every surviving borrow routed 'inspire' (clean-room).

rows.definition: newLoopDriveRegionHold resolves a `fak loop drive` run's region config (lane/tree, from loopDriveOptions flag overrides or the GOAL.md lane:/region: spec) and acquires a fenced, renewed lease hold on the leaseref fabric, refusing on a live overlapping lease (COLLISION_RISK) instead of racing it.
rows.distinction: Not loopDriveOptions itself (the plain config struct it reads as input) - newLoopDriveRegionHold is the constructor that turns that config into an actually-held, renewed lease over the drive's lifetime.

rows.definition: The super-loop registry is the curated, data-only set of named super loops (internal/superloop's unexported var registry, exposed by func Registry()) - the full collection an operator intent name (e.g. 'tend', 'improve-quality') resolves against, in declaration order.
rows.distinction: Not a single super loop instance/kind (the existing 'super loop' / KindSuperloop concept) - the registry is the whole named COLLECTION those instances are drawn from, and what Lookup/Names/Registry iterate over.

rows.definition: SurfaceLoop is the internal/laneadmit constant ("loop") tagging an admission Request as originating from a loop-type execution surface, distinguishing it from SurfaceDispatch and SurfaceManual requests in the shared lane-admission evidence vocabulary that internal/relay and internal/session also reference.
rows.distinction: Not defaultLoopPolicy (the loop/loop-drive admission POLICY file path) - SurfaceLoop is laneadmit's request-ORIGIN tag, unrelated to which policy file governs an admission decision.

rows.definition: TopLoop is the tuiLaneState JSON field (cmd/fak/tui_types.go) holding the highest-priority loop id rendered as a lane's headline in the fak TUI, set once per lane (first row wins) by cmd/fak/tui_loop_render.go alongside its companion TopLoopText summary.
rows.distinction: Not the unrelated internal/sessionaudit topLoop() helper in a different package, which trims a slice of SuccessLoopRow to its top N entries - they only share a spelling, not a concept.

rows.definition: topLoop is an internal/sessionaudit helper function that truncates a []SuccessLoopRow slice to its first n rows, used to cap a behavior report's SuccessLoops field to its top 10 entries.
rows.distinction: Not the TUI's TopLoop field (a single lane's headline loop id) - topLoop() here is a generic list-trimming function over an unrelated success-loop-row slice, in a different package.
